steps.explain: Sharks live in the ocean.
Sound travels uniquely far through ocean water.
Sound is the medium of music.
The Beatles are one of the greatest music acts in history.

fact: Sharks roam the ocean, where sound travels uniquely far — connecting acoustics to music, and the Fab Four.

steps.explain: A falling apple inspired Isaac Newton.
Newton's greatest discovery was the law of gravity.

fact: A falling apple inspired Isaac Newton to formulate the universal law of gravitation.

steps.explain: Trees are made of wood.
Wood pulp is pressed into paper.
Paper is what books are made of.

fact: Trees are felled for wood, processed into pulp, pressed into paper — the raw material of every book.

steps.explain: Lightning is a massive discharge of electricity.
Electricity flows through circuits.
Circuits are the heart of every computer.

fact: Lightning is raw electricity — harness it into circuits, and you have the heart of every computer.

steps.explain: A camera captures photographs.
Photographs are how we preserve memories.

fact: A camera freezes a moment into a photograph — and photographs are how humans preserve memories.

steps.explain: A compass enables navigation.
Navigation opened sea trade routes.

fact: The compass made accurate navigation possible, opening sea routes and centuries of global trade.

steps.explain: Feathers give birds the ability of flight.
Airplanes are humanity's mastery of flight.

fact: Birds' feathers inspired the dream of human flight — a dream the Wright Brothers made real in 1903.

steps.explain: Wind spins turbine blades.
Spinning turbines generate electricity.

fact: Wind spins turbine blades; spinning turbines generate electricity — the basis of all wind farms.

steps.explain: Bread shortages caused mass hunger.
Hunger drove desperate uprisings.
Uprisings escalated into full revolutions.

fact: Bread shortages caused hunger, hunger drove uprisings, and uprisings toppled regimes — from Paris 1789 onward.

steps.explain: The Harvest Moon lit farmers' fields at night.
Farmers harvested grain by moonlight.
Grain ground into flour makes pizza dough.

fact: The Harvest Moon lit fields for farmers; grain is their crop; and grain, ground to flour, gives us pizza dough.

steps.explain: Shakespeare's plays are filled with the sea.
The ocean's depths fascinated explorers.
Exploring depths led to the invention of submarines.

fact: Shakespeare's plays are filled with the sea and its mysteries; the ocean's depths fascinated explorers who built the submarine.

steps.explain: Penguins live on ice sheets.
Ice forms glaciers that grind rock.
Glaciers grind mountains into stone.
Massive stones were stacked to build pyramids.

fact: Penguins live on ice; glaciers grind mountains into stone; and massive stones, stacked by hand, became the pyramids.

steps.explain: Coffee drove global trade routes.
Trade demanded precise navigation.
Modern navigation is delivered by satellites.

fact: Coffee drove the Age of Exploration trade routes, which demanded precise navigation — eventually delivered by satellites.

steps.explain: Forests are full of plant species.
Many forest plants are medicinal herbs.
Herbs are the world's oldest source of medicine.

fact: Forests harbour thousands of plant species; many are medicinal herbs — the world's oldest pharmacy.

steps.explain: Rain fills rivers.
Rivers nurtured ancient civilizations.
Ancient civilizations gave us early democracy.

fact: Rain feeds rivers; rivers nurtured the ancient civilizations that gave us early democracy in Greece.

steps.explain: A seed grows into a plant.
Plants sustain animals.
Plants and animals together form an ecosystem.

fact: A seed grows into a plant; plants sustain animals; that web of plants and animals is an ecosystem.

steps.explain: Paint is the artist's primary tool.
Art's deepest purpose is to express emotion.

fact: Paint is the artist's tool; art's deepest purpose has always been to express and stir human emotion.

steps.explain: Violin strings vibrate at precise frequencies.
Frequency is a mathematical quantity.
Mathematics is the language of computers.

fact: Violin strings vibrate at precise frequencies; frequency is mathematical; and mathematics is the language of computers.

steps.explain: A key is used to unlock a coded lock.
Digital keys lock and unlock data via encryption.

fact: A key unlocks — in cryptography, a digital key is the mechanism that locks or unlocks data through encryption.

steps.explain: Digital maps rely on GPS.
GPS signals are broadcast by satellites.

fact: Maps became digital; digital maps rely on GPS; GPS signals are broadcast by satellites orbiting Earth.

steps.explain: Horses were the main form of transport for millennia.
The car replaced the horse as personal transport.

fact: Horses were humanity's engine for millennia — the 'horseless carriage' quite literally replaced them.

steps.explain: Mirrors bounce and direct light.
A laser is amplified, focused light.

fact: Mirrors bounce light; control light precisely enough — amplify and focus it — and you have a laser.

steps.explain: Accurate clocks solved the longitude problem for sailors.
Sailors could now confidently cross any ocean.

fact: Accurate marine clocks solved the longitude problem, giving sailors the tools to confidently cross any ocean.

steps.explain: Strong magnets can levitate objects.
Magnetic levitation powers maglev trains.

fact: Magnets repel as well as attract — powerful magnetic repulsion lifts maglev trains off the rails entirely.

steps.explain: Raindrops split sunlight into a rainbow spectrum.
A glass prism splits light the same way.

fact: Raindrops split sunlight into a rainbow's spectrum; a glass prism does exactly the same thing.

steps.explain: Newspapers established the daily news habit.
News moved from print to radio broadcast.
Broadcast news evolved into television.

fact: Newspapers established the habit of daily news; broadcasting extended it to radio, then to television.

steps.explain: A dam blocks and controls a river's flow.
Dams convert river flow into hydroelectric power.

fact: A dam harnesses the kinetic energy of river water, converting its flow into hydroelectric power.

steps.explain: The sun emits light.
Sunlight hits our skin.
Sunlight triggers vitamin D production in skin.

fact: Sunlight triggers the synthesis of vitamin D in human skin — the only vitamin your body can make itself.

steps.explain: Volcanoes produce lava when they erupt.
Cooled lava hardens into volcanic rock.
Volcanic rock weathers over time into fertile soil.

fact: Volcanic eruptions produce lava that cools into rock — and over centuries, volcanic rock weathers into some of the world's most fertile soil.

steps.explain: Silk gave its name to the ancient trade road.
The Silk Road was a vast trade network.
Trade routes were the original global network.
The internet is the modern global network.

fact: The Silk Road was humanity's first global network for exchanging goods and ideas — a forerunner of the internet.

steps.explain: High-altitude ice caps the world's mountains.
Melting mountain ice feeds streams.
Streams carry pure mountain water.
Clean water is the essential ingredient in whiskey.

fact: The purest whiskies trace their character to the clean mountain water used in distillation — ice melts, streams flow, whiskey pours.

steps.explain: Fire enabled cooking food.
Reliable food from cooking allowed permanent settlements.
Settlements grew into cities.

fact: Fire enabled cooking, which provided stable nutrition — freeing early humans to settle and build the first cities.

steps.explain: Clouds release rain.
Rain gathers and flows into rivers.

fact: Clouds are water vapour; rain falls from them; and rain collects in streams that grow into rivers.

steps.explain: Stars are studied through astronomy.
Astronomers tracked stars to determine seasons.
Tracking seasons gave us the calendar.

fact: Ancient peoples tracked stars to find seasonal patterns — those patterns became the first calendars.

steps.explain: The oldest musical instruments were bone flutes.
Flutes make music.
Keyboard music is played on keys.
Piano keys were once made from bone (ivory).

fact: The oldest instruments were bone flutes; eventually music evolved into keyboard instruments whose keys were once made from ivory.

steps.explain: Honey is made by bees.
Bees also produce beeswax.
Beeswax is the original candle material.

fact: Bees make both honey and beeswax — and beeswax candles have been humanity's light source for thousands of years.

steps.explain: Sand is mostly silicon dioxide.
Silicon is refined into microchips.
Microchips power computers and the internet.

fact: Ordinary beach sand contains silicon dioxide — refined into silicon wafers that become the microchips powering the internet.

steps.explain: Eggs hatch into chickens.
Raising chickens was an early form of agriculture.
Agriculture created food surpluses.
Food surpluses funded armies and built empires.

fact: Domesticating animals created food surpluses — surpluses funded armies, and armies built empires.

steps.explain: Snow accumulates on mountains.
Snow builds up immense weight on slopes.
Too much weight causes a snow avalanche.

fact: Snow packs onto mountain slopes; once enough weight accumulates, the whole mass slides down as an avalanche.

steps.explain: Ink is used for printing.
Printing enabled cheap political pamphlets.
Pamphlets spread political propaganda rapidly.
Propaganda fuelled revolutions across history.

fact: Ink enabled printing, printing made pamphlets cheap, and pamphlets spread the radical ideas that ignited revolutions.
